clue.text: Underground supporter

parts.note: read literally, something that holds up the roof below ground in a mine, not a fan of the London Tube

explanation.surface: A fan of the London Tube, or someone backing a secret resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine shaft's roof is held up by timber props, so a prop in a coal pit supports work underground.

clue.text: City couple with fever

parts.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair, a couple
ague is an old word for a shivering fever such as malaria

explanation.surface: A city where a pair of travellers come down with a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital of the Czech Republic, an example of a city.

clue.text: String of invective from one in business

indicators.note: in tells us the word for one is placed inside the word for business

parts.note: trade is commerce, business
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in commerce unleashes a stream of abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is a rant, a stream of abusive words.

clue.text: Salesman with an allowance to make amends

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
an gives the indefinite article A
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or goods

explanation.surface: A salesman is given a payment to compensate for a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation for a wrong done, the making good of an injury.

clue.text: Songster, it went after seed

indicators.note: went after says the word it is placed behind the word for seed in the charade

parts.note: a pip is a small fruit seed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singing bird chases after some seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird, so a bird that sings, a songster.

clue.text: Not in favour with Jack getting between one of the breakwaters that is not fixed

indicators.note: getting between says the next letters are pushed into the middle of the breakwater word

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
V, short for versus, means against, not in favour
a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor

explanation.surface: An opponent and a sailor squeeze between harbour walls that can shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' as a sailor is a crossword convention; 'getting between' is the container signal, and the definition is the whole closing phrase 'that is not fixed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being moved is portable, not set in one place.

clue.text: Lady about to be included, one on a tree

indicators.note: to be included says the word for about goes inside the word for lady

parts.note: madam is a polite address to a lady
CA is circa, Latin for about
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman about to join someone perched up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian nut-bearing evergreen is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Individual in the forefront is conceited

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for individual sits inside the word for forefront

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the forefront
I can stand for one, an individual

explanation.surface: Someone who always pushes to the front is full of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud of one's looks, self-admiring, is a synonym of conceited.

clue.text: Resent move with Reg performing inside

indicators.note: inside puts the jumbled name within the word for move

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of Reg are acting up, rearranged

explanation.surface: Bitterness at being shifted while Reg takes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' is the anagram signal for the name Reg, and 'inside' places the scrambled name within the word for move.
explanation.definitionFit: To grudge or envy something given to another is to resent it.

clue.text: Camera's revelation?

parts.note: a camera reveals film to light for a set time, and also may lay bare a scandal

explanation.surface: A hidden camera exposes something scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: The light let onto film by a shutter, and also the unmasking of a scandal.

clue.text: Aweigh — an excursion

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
a trip is an outing, an excursion

explanation.surface: Anchors up, off on an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: A nautical term: an anchor that has just been lifted clear of the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for an anchor just clear of the seabed, raised and hanging.

clue.text: Gathering it's improving

explanation.surface: A crop being harvested as the weather gets better.
explanation.definitionFit: Collecting things up from the ground, and recovering or getting better, as trade does.

clue.text: Don't learn enough from reserve player

explanation.surface: A substitute actor who never bothered learning the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, too little learning; as one, an actor ready to replace a lead.

clue.text: Transport, say, with kiss

indicators.note: say signals the word for transport is heard, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A peck on the cheek on the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a smacking kiss.

clue.text: He had not been invited to cover the runner

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to cover with earth
a loper is one who runs with long strides

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher being tucked in by the athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder who pushes into places uninvited.

clue.text: Dramatic supervisor

parts.note: not a flamboyant boss but the person overseeing the running of a theatre production backstage

explanation.surface: A boss given to theatrical outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running the backstage side of a play, overseeing the theatre crew.

clue.text: Indication of queue of girls in uniform?

parts.note: a Guide is a member of the Girl Guides, a uniformed youth movement
a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Is that a row of Girl Guides standing in formation?
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or pointer showing how to proceed.

clue.text: One payment and another, rupees included, were not taxed

parts.note: scot is an old word for a payment or tax

indicators.note: included says the rupee letter goes into the second payment word

parts.note: a fee is another payment

explanation.surface: Two payments in Indian currency that escaped the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: Without penalty or charge; originally exempt from the scot tax.

clue.text: Finish in the end surrounded

indicators.note: in says the word for finish sits inside the word for the end

parts.note: taken as the word end
a close is a finish, an ending

explanation.surface: In the end, cornered and finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut in on all sides, fenced around.

clue.text: Odd sectional parts merged

indicators.note: parts as a verb means splits up, so the letters of the two words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Strange sections of something were joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined into one unit, as companies or debts are.

clue.text: Drink to sing about

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of to sing are moved around

explanation.surface: Having a drink before bursting into song.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong old English ale, so a drink.

clue.text: Channel in wooded area contains nothing

indicators.note: contains says the wooded area holds the letter for nothing

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A ditch in the woods with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow cut or furrow, a channel.

clue.text: Sounds like the end of the account

indicators.note: Sounds like says the word for the end is heard, giving another spelling

parts.note: a tail is the end part of something

explanation.surface: The end of the story is near.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or narrative, an account of events.

clue.text: Opening I left, working out rota for respirator

parts.note: a vent is an opening for air

indicators.note: working out suggests the letters of rota are sorted out into a new order

explanation.surface: A hospital rota is drawn up for a breathing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' turns ROTA into ATOR to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that breathes for a patient, a breathing apparatus.

clue.text: One continental with twitch outside had military jacket

indicators.note: outside says the twitch word goes around the continental one

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A European soldier with a nervous twitch wore a uniform coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting uniform coat worn by soldiers or police.

clue.text: Mark left on cliff

explanation.surface: A sign left on a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: The trace a healed wound leaves, and a steep rocky outcrop or crag.

clue.text: Cutting away, are removing a part

indicators.note: removing says the following letter is dropped from the word are

parts.note: a section is a part

explanation.surface: Surgeons are removing part of an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical operation cutting out part of an organ or tissue.

clue.text: Horse in top form

indicators.note: form as a verb means to shape, so the letters of in top are reshaped

explanation.surface: A racehorse at the peak of its form.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald or spotted pony, an American horse.

clue.text: Some recommend or seek support

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice on whether to recommend something or look for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or approve publicly, to vouch for.

clue.text: Oxidise metal bar in centre

indicators.note: in tells us the word for bar sits inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: Rust eating away at a metal bar from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat away by chemical action, as rust does to iron.
